newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were narrowly mixed but bond prices were slightly lower. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.13/2.08 percent compared with Monday's yield of 2.18/2.13 percent.
One-year closed at a yield of 2.43/2.38 percent against Monday's yield of 2.13/2.08 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$97.95/98.00 from Monday's close of S$98.20/98.25, September 2001 at S$96.95/97.00 versus S$97.53/97.58 and June 2003 at S$94.92/94.97 against S$95.50/95.55.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Monday's 3-5/8 3-1/2 percent.
